title: Give each rule id a spoken line and state the invocation law
action:
Two edits, per pstack-gaps D4 and D5.

EDIT 1 — the spoken forms. In docs/knowledge/areas/doctrine-layer/router-triage-and-the-agents-md-duplication-boundary.md, section `## AGENTS.md rule homes`, every one of the ten rules already has a row shaped `- \`<rule-id>\` (AGENTS.md § <section>):` followed by an indented `- applied_at:` block. Add to EACH of the ten rows one INDENTED line, placed directly under the row and BEFORE its `applied_at:` line, shaped exactly:

  spoken: <one plain sentence, in the words a person would say>

CRITICAL CONSTRAINT: the line MUST be indented (two spaces) and MUST NOT start with `- ` or `* ` at column 0. Read `parse_agents_rule_homes` in packages/bee-rs/crates/bee/src/verbs/knowledge/ownership.rs first: it treats any line starting with a dash as a NEW rule row, so a sibling bullet would make `bee knowledge check` report twenty rules instead of ten. Prove it afterwards by running `.bee/bin/bee knowledge check --json` and confirming the rule count is still ten and no new `duplicate_rule_home` or `unknown_rule_ref` finding appeared.

Write each spoken line as the sentence a user would actually say out loud, not a restatement of the id. Keep it one line, under 110 characters, no trailing period needed. The ten ids are agents-review-user-invoked, agents-gates-never-self-approved, agents-worktree-first, agents-proof-at-cap, agents-never-build-on-red, agents-never-zero-execution-workers, agents-capture-line-at-close, agents-one-next-action, agents-context-handoff-65, agents-one-commit-per-cell. Derive each sentence from that rule's own AGENTS.md section — read the section, do not guess from the id.

EDIT 2 — the invocation law. In packages/bee/AGENTS.block.md add ONE short paragraph, in ONE place only, stating: a user may invoke any rule id by name mid-run ('apply never-build-on-red'); the agent resolves the id in the rule index at docs/knowledge/areas/doctrine-layer/router-triage-and-the-agents-md-duplication-boundary.md (`## AGENTS.md rule homes`), applies it to the work in hand, and the reply MUST name the decision or step the rule changed — or state plainly that it changed nothing. Never a bare acknowledgement. Place it where the surrounding contract already talks about rules or communication; keep it under 6 lines and match the file's voice. Then run `.bee/bin/bee dev regen` so AGENTS.md and every generated copy carry the same paragraph — do NOT hand-edit AGENTS.md.

Do not add a CLI verb, a new file, or a second index.

REGEN, inside this cell and in this order: `.bee/bin/bee dev render-skill-trees`, then `.bee/bin/bee onboard --repo-root . --apply`, then `.bee/bin/bee dev release-manifest --write`. Commit the regenerated copies with the change; a hand-edited generated copy is a defect.
verify: `rg -c 'spoken:' docs/knowledge/areas/doctrine-layer/router-triage-and-the-agents-md-duplication-boundary.md` returns 10. `.bee/bin/bee knowledge check --json` still reports exactly ten homed rules with no new duplicate_rule_home or unknown_rule_ref finding. The invocation law appears in packages/bee/AGENTS.block.md and, after `.bee/bin/bee dev regen`, in AGENTS.md, and both name the index path. `git diff --stat` shows AGENTS.md changed by regen, never by hand. `.bee/bin/bee dev release-manifest --check` is clean.

truths: All ten rule rows in the `## AGENTS.md rule homes` section carry a non-empty indented `spoken:` line, placed before their `applied_at:` line.
No spoken line starts with `- ` or `* ` at column 0, so `parse_agents_rule_homes` still reads exactly ten rules.
`bee knowledge check` reports the same ten homed rules as before, with no new duplicate_rule_home or unknown_rule_ref finding.
Each spoken line is derived from that rule's own AGENTS.md section, not paraphrased from its id.
packages/bee/AGENTS.block.md states the invocation law once, naming the index path and requiring the reply to name what the rule changed or say plainly that it changed nothing.
AGENTS.md carries the same paragraph and reached it through the regen chain, never a hand edit.
